storyNotes.originalText: Jacob's family grew into the nation of Israel. They FILLED the land of Egypt.
storyNotes.cleanText: Jacob’s family grew into a huge nation called Israel. They filled the land of Egypt.

storyNotes.originalText: Egypt's king was afraid of them. He made them work hard as SLAVES, but they kept growing.
storyNotes.cleanText: Pharaoh made the Israelites work hard as slaves, but their families kept growing.

storyNotes.originalText: Pharaoh ordered two midwives to kill the baby BOYS, but they refused to do what he asked.
storyNotes.cleanText: Two midwives, Shiphrah and Puah, refused Pharaoh’s order to kill the Hebrew baby boys.

storyNotes.originalText: Pharaoh gave a new order: "Throw all the Hebrew baby boys in the Nile RIVER!"
storyNotes.cleanText: Pharaoh ordered the Hebrew baby boys to be thrown into the Nile River.

storyNotes.originalText: An Israelite family had a baby boy. They kept him HIDDEN for three months.
storyNotes.cleanText: An Israelite family hid their baby boy for three months.

storyNotes.originalText: She put him in a BASKET and placed him in the grass by the river. His sister watched nearby.
storyNotes.cleanText: The baby's mother put him in a basket by the river while his sister watched nearby.

storyNotes.originalText: Pharaoh's daughter found the basket in the river. She felt SORRY for him.
storyNotes.cleanText: Pharaoh’s daughter found the baby in the basket and felt sorry for him.

questions.question: What made old Abe’s family so special?
questions.answer: God gave him a whole pile of promises.

questions.question: Had God kept that promise?
questions.answer: Yes.

questions.question: Why?
questions.answer: There would be more of them than Egyptians; maybe they’d join their enemies in a fight against them.
questions.notes: Keep source question; needs surrounding context or is quoted dialogue, not a standalone worksheet item.

questions.question: But did this new Pharaoh remember Joseph at all?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What evil plan did Pharaoh come up with?
questions.answer: Turn the Israelites into slaves; make them work hard.

questions.question: Did Pharaoh’s plan stop the Israelites from growing?
questions.answer: No; they grew even faster.

questions.question: What evil order did Pharaoh give to these women?
questions.answer: Kill the Hebrew baby boys.

questions.question: What was Pharaoh’s third evil plan to stop the Israelites?
questions.answer: Every Hebrew boy born must be tossed into the river.

questions.question: Why?
questions.answer: Pharaoh ordered baby boys to be tossed in the river.
questions.notes: Keep source question; needs surrounding context or is quoted dialogue, not a standalone worksheet item.

questions.question: So what did they do?
questions.notes: Keep source question; needs surrounding context or is quoted dialogue, not a standalone worksheet item.

questions.question: What evil order had Pharaoh given to the Israelites?
questions.answer: To put every Hebrew baby boy into the Nile River.

questions.question: Who was sent on a secret spying mission to make sure her little brother was okay?
questions.answer: His older sister.

questions.question: Do you want me to go and get one of the Hebrew women?
questions.notes: Keep source question; needs surrounding context or is quoted dialogue, not a standalone worksheet item.

questions.question: Who found the little baby boat floating in the Nile River?
questions.answer: Pharaoh’s daughter.

questions.question: What did her dad want done with Israelite baby boys?
questions.answer: Thrown into the river.

questions.question: Should I find a Hebrew woman to feed this baby?
questions.notes: Keep source question; needs surrounding context or is quoted dialogue, not a standalone worksheet item.

questions.question: What did Pharaoh's daughter say?
questions.answer: Yes, and I'll pay her.

questions.question: After that, what happened?
questions.answer: He became the son of Pharaoh’s daughter.

questions.question: What did she name her adopted son?
questions.answer: Moses.

questions.question: So how does the story of the birth of Moses teach us, strengthen us, encourage us, or give us hope?
questions.notes: Keep source question; needs surrounding context or is quoted dialogue, not a standalone worksheet item.

questions.question: Why?
questions.answer: Because God was with them!
questions.notes: Keep source question; needs surrounding context or is quoted dialogue, not a standalone worksheet item.

questions.question: Guess who?
questions.answer: Jesus.

questions.question: And what do these words tell us?
questions.answer: That God can do whatever he pleases.

questions.question: What happened to Jacob’s family by the beginning of Exodus?
questions.answer: They had grown into a great nation

questions.question: Because he was afraid of them, what did Pharaoh do?
questions.answer: Made the Israelites work hard as slaves

questions.question: What happened after Pharaoh made the Israelites his slaves?
questions.answer: They grew even more

questions.question: What did Pharaoh tell the midwives to do? What happened?
questions.answer: To kill the baby boys; they didn’t obey him

questions.question: What final order did Pharaoh give?
questions.answer: Throw the baby boys into the river

questions.question: What did the couple from the tribe of Levi do with their baby boy?
questions.answer: Hid him for three months

questions.question: When they couldn’t hide him anymore, what did they do?
questions.answer: Placed him in a basket in the Nile River

questions.question: Who found the baby? How did she feel?
questions.answer: Pharaoh’s daughter; she felt sorry for him

questions.question: What did the baby’s sister Miriam say?
questions.answer: Do you want me to find someone to feed him?

questions.question: After he no longer needed his mother’s milk, what happened to the boy?
questions.answer: He became the son of Pharaoh’s daughter; she named him Moses

reviewFlags.text: Source lesson quotes Psalm 135:6 from ESV. Proposed BSB wording reads “The LORD does all that pleases Him in the heavens and on the earth, in the seas and in all their depths.” Confirm full-verse wording, translation choice and distribution clearance.

The source describes Pharaoh ordering the killing of Hebrew baby boys. Check child-facing Multiple Choice, True/False, Finish Story and caption wording for age appropriateness without changing biblical meaning.
Approve or edit the 12 newly composed incorrect Multiple Choice answer choices, seven proposed false facts and Odd Words/Checkboxes unrelated words before publication.
Review the six intentionally incorrect claims and their correction keys. The child-facing paragraph uses simple wording.
Seven Story Notes are preserved verbatim. Adapted cleanText and narrative captions should be checked against the original chronology and terminology.
Confirm the four small drawing scene candidates are clear, central to the story, fun and appropriate for children.
The ten selected facts are distinct for Sort the Story (eight), True/False (one) and True/False Maze (one). Live Presets 1–3 and generator output have not been tested.
Nine child-friendly Crossword answers and clues were prepared but grid feasibility and intersections require the real generator.
The source uses a lower-case display font for God in its Big Idea. The prepared Big Idea capitalizes God and preserves the meaning.
The source names the baby Moses near the end and identifies his older sister as Miriam later in the teaching narrative. Review whether early use of these names is suitable for your worksheets.
